newsitem.title: BURMA: Burmese temple bomb explosion kills four.
newsitem.headline: Burmese temple bomb explosion kills four.

text.p: Two time bombs exploded at a Buddhist religious site on the outskirts of the Burmese capital Rangoon late on Wednesday, killing four people and wounding 18, a government spokesman said on Thursday.

The bombs detonated as hordes of pilgrims were paying homage to the Buddhist Sacred Tooth Relic that had been brought to Burma from China. All the deaths and injuries were caused by the second explosion, official media reported.

One security officer, a Red Cross worker and two members of the government-sponsored Union Solidarity and Development Association (USDA) were killed in the blast at the Kaba Aye and Maha Pasana Cave about 4.5 km (seven miles) from Rangoon.
A spokesman for the military government told Reuters that the blasts were being investigated.
"Investigation into the explosions is still going on and we would be able to have a better idea of who did it after the investigation is completed," he said.

Burma's ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC), which took power in 1988, has faced renewed unrest in the past month when students staged two weeks of street protests. It also faces ethnic guerrilla armies such as the Karen in eastern Burma.

Neighbouring China is one of a handful of countries to maintain close ties to the SLORC, which has been accused by western nations of widespread human rights abuses, including restrictions on Nobel Peace Laureate Aung San Suu Kyi.

The explosions on Wednesday were the first reported in or around Rangoon since a bomb went off outside the U.S. embassy in the capital in July. No one was hurt in that incident, which the SLORC blamed on "destructionists", and no group claimed responsibility.

Official media said the bombs were planted by "a group of dastardly destructive elements" and aimed at harming the ties between Burma and China as well as to cause "terror and anxiety among the people".

The harmless, first blast exploded in the Kaba Aye Pagoda area. But as officials were investigating, a second bomb exploded inside a vase near where flowers were being offered at the Maha Pasana Cave, the New Light of Myanmar reported.
The Sacred Tooth Relic, believed to be the original tooth of Lord Buddha, was brought to Burma on December 6 from China and was not damaged in the blasts, the media reported.
The New Light of Myanmar said seven security officers, one Red Cross member, four USDA members, one member of the Sangha (religious body) and five pilgrims were injured.
Top officials of the SLORC and the Chinese ambassador to Burma went to the scene of the blast for inspection, it said.

"It is learnt that such an explosion was due to the planting of a timed mine by the group of dastardly destructive elements with extremely wicked and ruthless intent to harm the friendship between China and Myanmar (Burma), disrupt the stability in the country... ," the newspaper said.
"There was no damage whatsover to the Sacred Tooth Relic," it added.
The government spokesman said those who had set up the bombs for explosion must have been desperate because they had done it at a religious place where many worshippers had congregated.
"Whoever did this must be very desparate to create problems. It is so cruel to do it in a place where people had been gathering for religious purposes," he said.
The spokesman said that the line of pilgrims at the Maha Pasana Cave Hall was about one mile (kilometre) long and the place was packed with pilgrims.
